checks: Compared the full raw files byte for byte. The only difference is one dollar sign added to close the p(R) display. The display is correctly paired, all other statement text matches, and the proof and all metadata are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Checked all cyclic consecutive and next-neighbor determinants are 1 in the six canonical directions; successive gaps are strictly below π. The exact realization matrix has the stated entries, including wraparound and all zero nonadjacent entries.

The diagonal PSD bounds give R_i²≥1/(c_{i−1}+c_i), and radii are positive. The subsequent core bound R_iR_{i+1}≤2W_i then bounds R_i above using the already proved positive lower bound on R_{i+1}. No possible limit reaches the excluded zero-radius boundary.

The feasible vectors are exactly the intersection of the positive compact box with the closed product inequalities and inverse image of the closed PSD cone under the continuous matrix map. Nonemptiness follows from the assumed actual body, and the converse criterion supplies a polygon at every feasible vector.

All chord length denominators are positive in the box. The continuous weight therefore attains its minimum on this feasible set. A positive radius increment at either target node missing both incident cores preserves W and strictly improves the weight by the same-batch saturation theorem.
Verified the raw source digest of 50872e565640d12b and checked §1. The finite-data compactness and attainment argument and the two incident-core conditions match the cited section.

dependencies.mapping: The canonical six rays and finite sector areas satisfy the geometric hypotheses. Core products and PSD characterize the positive radius vectors in both directions, and the realization can be polygonal.

With the six sector areas fixed, there is room for a small increase at node 1 or 4 whenever its two incident inequalities are strict. Opposite endpoint and other chord lengths stay fixed, and the canonical normalized inverse weight strictly decreases.
